explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/97: does every convex polygon have a vertex with no other 4 vertices equidistant from it? The proposition is formalised correctly: for every nonempty convex-independent finite A ⊆ ℝ², ¬HasNEquidistantProperty 4 A, where the property says every p ∈ A has ≥ 4 points of A on some circle of radius r > 0 around it. However the page now records that 'This is false': for all large n there is a convex polygon in which every vertex has ≫ log log n vertices at distance 1, with a formalised proof linked. So the answer is no. Under the @[question] convention the statement should be negated and recategorised as solved; as written (tagged open, unnegated) it is a false statement. The formalisation of the question is right; its status and documentation are out of date.
